## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Lokuttarakathā* ("Discussion of the Transcendent") is the eighth treatise in the second major division (*Yuganaddhavagga*) of the *Paṭisambhidāmagga* (*Ps* 2.8) in the Khuddaka Nikāya. The treatise provides an analytical exposition of phenomena that are supramundane or world-transcending (*lokuttara*) [Buddhist Philosophy and Meditation Practice 2012]. As cited in secondary literature, the text establishes the definition of the term by explaining that the noble paths transcend the world (*ariyamaggā lokaṁ uttarantīti lokuttarā*), whereas the fruits of ascetic life (*sāmaññaphalāni*) and Nibbāna have already transcended the world (*lokato uttiṇṇāti lokuttarā*) [Buddhist Philosophy and Meditation Practice 2012]. The text classifies as transcendent the thirty-seven requisites of awakening (*bodhipakkhiyā dhammā*)—comprising the four foundations of mindfulness (*satipaṭṭhāna*), four right strivings (*sammappadhāna*), four bases of spiritual power (*iddhipāda*), five faculties (*indriya*), five powers (*bala*), seven factors of awakening (*bojjhaṅga*), and the noble eightfold path—together with the four noble paths, the four fruits of asceticism, and Nibbāna [Buddhist Philosophy and Meditation Practice 2012].

 DharmaNexus algorithmic matching identifies 59 Pali-internal text-reuse passages across eight texts, with no cross-language alignments meeting threshold criteria [DharmaNexus]. The largest concentration of shared textual material is with the *Dhammasaṅgaṇi* (*Dukaatthuddhāra*, Ds 2.4.2; *Tikaatthuddhāra*, Ds 2.4.1) and its commentary (*Dhammasaṅgaṇi-aṭṭhakathā*), as well as the text's own commentary (*Paṭisambhidāmagga-aṭṭhakathā*) [DharmaNexus]. Textual segments are also shared with the *Sāmagāma Sutta* (MN 104), the *Cūḷaniddesa* (Cnd 23), the *Mahāniddesa* (Mnd 14), and the *Milindapañha* (Mil 3.1.13) [DharmaNexus].
